additional_info.subject: ID0458727-DC/Si-D/NL-[MP / P4 170000481] Faulted chargers CRM:03042000088
additional_info.body:
Dear Service Coordinator / RC,
I am writing to inform that we are moving the case
0458727
﻿from the Technical Support to the eMobility RC-NL SI E Queue. The first response has been sent to the customer, and we kindly ask you to take over the case and perform the necessary troubleshooting steps.
Customer:
Product:
Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset:
MP / P4 170000481
Charger ID / Serial No.:
Charger address/functional location:
Priority:
Medium
Possible solution:
As the client reported to us, the problem is related to TB18 and FC23, and one of these may need replacement.
We need you to:
Check the 12V circuit.
Identify where any voltage drop occurs.
Take the necessary steps for replacement.
If
FC23
is tripping, it might be due to a short circuit in any of the circuits shown in the screenshots. I will send these screenshots of the 12V circuit to guide you in the check
Kindly pick up the case using "Pick" option in the queue or manually using the "Assign" function from the
eMobility RC-NL SI E Queue
and work on it & document the activity (Logs/Field Service Report) and attach it to the case under documents Tab on ISP.
In case you require expert support, kindly create Work-order as per
unified service process
. If you need assistance with ordering Expert Support, feel free to reach out to Sousa, Afonso (SI E CS SD) at
afonso-sousa@siemens.com
or Teodoso, Rui (SI E CS SD ES) at
rui.teodoso@siemens.com
.
Kindly close the case post resolution following the case handling guidelines.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Technical Support Team –
Younes Baroudi
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.

additional_info.subject: Site visit
additional_info.body:
FC23 was tripped on arrival. Reset FC23 and performed a hard reset on SiChargeD.
Charger came back online with all outlet available. Outlet 3 (CCS2 plug on SiChargeD) was used for testing and verified to be working.
The AC plug voltage monitoring device error LED is lit up.
+F10-CA1 8EM5903-0AA00-1AA4 1 VOLTAGE MONITORING DEVICE
